members.universe: NSE sectoral index constituents (top 2 liquid stocks per sector)
members.thesis: Intraday sector rotation in Indian markets follows a predictable pattern: the strongest performing sector in the first hour tends to continue outperforming through midday, but reverts in the last hour. entry_long: stock_close > stock_VWAP (momentum phase) OR stock_close < stock_VWAP (reversion phase)
entry_short: stock_close < stock_VWAP (momentum phase) OR stock_close > stock_VWAP (reversion phase)
members.exit_target: 30 bps from entry (momentum phase), 25 bps (reversion phase)
filters: India_VIX < 22; skip in high-vol (all sectors correlated, rotation fails)
wait until 10:15 for first-hour ranking data
momentum phase: NIFTY 50 directional (not range-bound); reversion phase: any
weaknesses: On strong trending days (macro events, global risk-on/off), all sectors move together and rotation signals generate noise. The 30 bps minimum dispersion filter helps but doesn't eliminate this.
The 13:30 switch from momentum to reversion is arbitrary and may not align with actual flow patterns, which vary by day of week and proximity to expiry.
Using single stocks as sector proxies introduces idiosyncratic risk — a stock-specific event can distort sector-level signal.

members.name: sector_rotation_intraday_v1
members.thesis: Intraday sector rotation follows a predictable pattern: sectors that lead in the first hour often continue leading, while laggards mean-revert during lunch hour and underperformers catch up in the final hour. This pattern is driven by institutional portfolio rebalancing: morning flow is directional
entry_long: AM session (10:15-12:00): go long top 2 sectors by sector_rank (momentum)
PM session (13:00-15:15): go long bottom 2 sectors by sector_return_from_open (mean reversion)
entry_short: AM session: short bottom 2 sectors by sector_rank
PM session: short top 2 sectors by sector_return_from_open
filters: sector must have > ₹100Cr aggregate turnover in first hour
for AM momentum: only if nifty50 is not down > 0.5% (not a crash day)
skip if avg spread of top 3 sector stocks > 0.1%
weaknesses: Sector rotation patterns are noisy and may not hold in macro-driven markets where all sectors move together
Multiple positions across sectors means higher total capital at risk
PM mean reversion assumes morning overperformers give back gains — but sometimes trends persist all day
members.prior_art: Intraday sector rotation — institutional portfolio construction concept. Academic support: Moskowitz & Grinblatt (1999) industry momentum.
